newsitem.title: THAILAND: Floods raise Thai rice prices.
newsitem.headline: Floods raise Thai rice prices.

text.p: Thai rice prices firmed this week after monsoon floods prompted the agriculture ministry to trim its forecast of Thailand's main crop, trade sources said on Thursday.

They said market sentiment was bouyed by upcoming Japanese rice tenders on Thursday and next month, Syria's planned tender next month, and news that Sri Lanka plans to import more than 500,000 tonnes this year to cover its domestic shortfall.

Thai 100 percent B benchmark was quoted at about $330-350 per tonne Free On Board (FOB) Bangkok against $330-340 last week. Thai 100 percent fragrant rice was quoted at about $615 on the same basis against $605 last week.
"Tighter supply pushed prices up. But we haven't heard of any new major orders. Just small orders from regular customers," said a Thai exporter.
"Our prices are higher than those of Vietnam on an average of $30 per tonne...not very attractive," said another trader.
The agriculture ministry this week cut its projection of the 1996/97 (May/January) main paddy (unhusked rice) crop to 17.60 million tonnes from an 18.11 million forecast in July.
Some traders discounted the ministry's lower crop forecast, saying the expected flood damage would likely be offset by post-flood replanting.
Thai traders expected to win part of the Japanese Food Agency's 110,000-tonne tender later on Thursday.
"There is some good news on demand from Japan and Sri Lanka but whether they will buy from us or not remained to be seen," said another trader.
Syria will next month tender for 12,000 tonnes for January shipment with results expected on November 20.
Ships are loading 55,400 tonnes of rice at river piers near Bangkok this week for Asian, Mideast and African markets.

The loading included 12,000 tonnes of 100 percent grade to Syria, 10,000 tonnes of 100 percent grade to Iran, 13,800 tonnes of 25 percent grade to India, 10,000 tonnes of parboiled rice to Africa, and the rest to unidentified destinations.
The commerce ministry said Thailand exported 4.16 million tonnes of rice during January 1-October 13 against 4.73 million a year ago.
